title: Customer Service Advisor
description:
EE Merthyr Tydfil Contact Centre - Full-time role - 37.5 Hours per week

If you're outgoing, full of energy and love talking to people, you'd be better off in sales with EE.

Maybe you've worked in retail, or hospitality before. You know how to deal with customers but you're looking for something more exciting - a job that's going to challenge you. And, of course, you want to earn a bit more cash.

Our team in Merthyr is full of people like you - so you'll be in great company here.

What does being a sales advisor involve?

You'll join a lively sales team in our Merthyr contact centre. We'll train you to take incoming calls from existing EE customers and help them find the best deals on their phones and broadband. You'll also help them to navigate the different tech products we sell.

You need to be a great listener as well as a fluent talker. A lot of the time, you'll pick up on something that someone has said, then use that to match them with the perfect product.

Forget what you've heard about sales

Don't let what you've heard about sales put you off. Let's smash a few myths
- Yes, there are targets to hit. But the kind of people who like sales, love that. You're probably naturally competitive. You get a buzz out of beating the person next to you. You hate being bored at work.
- It's not "cold calling". The calls come in to you and you decide how best you can help the customer. That's why we value resourceful people who like fixing problems.
- People say it's "hard selling". It's really not! You're basically talking to people about fun tech stuff that they already want. Who doesn't love a better phone, faster broadband or a new console?

Why you'll be better off at EE

GREAT MONEY - you start on £26,116 which goes up to £26,738 after 8 months.

UNCAPPED COMMISSION - the more you sell, the more you can earn.

BRILLIANT BENEFITS - including 24/7 GP appointments for you and your family, free parking and discounts on EE products like phones and broadband that could save you £100s every year.

GROWTH - we're passionate about developing our people. There are plenty of career paths across EE and BT.

FLEXIBILITY - you can bank hours then take time off when you need. Plus, generous leave for carers and anyone starting a family.

GREAT PEOPLE - you're working with people like you. It's a sociable, supportive environment.

title: Wellbeing & Volunteer Coordinator
description:
Wellbeing and Volunteer Coordinator

Marauders Men's Health Charity
Hours: 20 hours per week (part-time)
Salary: £26,520 per annum pro rata
Location: Remote
Contract: Fixed-term until March 2028
Responsible to: CEO

About Marauders Men's Health Charity

Marauders Men's Health Charity is committed to improving the health and wellbeing of men and creating opportunities for men to connect, build supportive relationships and access the help they need.

We recognise that men can face significant barriers to talking about their mental and physical health. Through our activities, support, volunteering and community engagement, we aim to create welcoming, inclusive spaces where men feel able to participate, connect and thrive.

We are looking for a passionate and organised Wellbeing and Volunteer Coordinator to play a key role in supporting our wellbeing activities and developing our volunteer network.

The Role

The Wellbeing and Volunteer Coordinator will be responsible for coordinating and developing Marauders' wellbeing activities while supporting, recruiting and engaging volunteers across the charity.

This is a varied and rewarding role for someone who enjoys working with people, building relationships and creating positive opportunities within the community.

You will be an important point of contact for volunteers and participants, helping to ensure that our activities are safe, welcoming, inclusive and responsive to the needs of the men we support.

The successful candidate will be confident working independently, but also enjoy being part of a small, committed team. You will need excellent communication and organisational skills, a positive attitude and a genuine commitment to improving men's health and wellbeing.

Key Responsibilities

Wellbeing Coordination
- Coordinate and support the delivery of Marauders' wellbeing activities, groups, sessions and events.
- Help develop activities that encourage men to improve their physical, mental and social wellbeing.
- Create a welcoming and inclusive environment where participants feel comfortable and valued.
- Build positive relationships with participants and identify opportunities to improve their experience.
- Monitor attendance patterns and personally connect with disengaged members to provide targeted encouragement and support.
- Work with the CEO to develop wellbeing plans for beneficiaries
- Gather feedback from participants and use this to inform the development of activities and services.
- Assist with planning, promoting and evaluating wellbeing programmes and events.

Volunteer Coordination
- Recruit, welcome, support and retain volunteers across the charity.
- Develop positive and supportive relationships with volunteers.
- Coordinate volunteer rotas, roles and activities.
- Ensure volunteers receive appropriate induction, guidance, training and ongoing support.
- Help volunteers understand their roles, responsibilities and boundaries.
- Recognise and celebrate volunteer contributions.
- Maintain accurate volunteer records and ensure relevant checks, documentation and training are kept up to date.
- Identify opportunities for volunteers to develop new skills and take on additional responsibilities.
- Organise volunteer meetings, briefings and opportunities for feedback.
- Support the development of a positive, inclusive and rewarding volunteer culture.

Community Engagement
- Build relationships with local organisations, community groups and relevant services.
- Promote Marauders' activities and volunteering opportunities within the local community.
- Attend community events and represent the charity in a professional and positive manner.
- Help identify opportunities to reach men who may benefit from Marauders' support.
- Support partnership working with organisations involved in men's health, wellbeing and community development.

Administration, Monitoring and Safeguarding
- Maintain accurate records relating to participants, volunteers and activities.
- Support monitoring and evaluation of projects and services.
- Contribute to reports, funding applications and evidence of impact where required.
- Follow Marauders' policies and procedures, including safeguarding, health and safety, equality and diversity, confidentiality and data protection.
- Identify and appropriately report safeguarding or wellbeing concerns in line with organisational procedures.
- Support risk assessments and ensure activities are delivered safely.
- Undertake other reasonable duties that support the effective operation and development of the charity.

Person Specification

Essential
- Experience of working with people in a community, voluntary, wellbeing, health or support setting.
- Experience of coordinating volunteers, activities, groups or community projects.
- Excellent interpersonal and communication skills.
- Ability to build trust and positive relationships with people from a wide range of backgrounds.
- Strong organisational skills and the ability to manage competing priorities.
- Confidence working independently and using initiative.
- Good written and verbal communication skills.
- A non-judgemental, empathetic and inclusive approach.
- An understanding of the importance of men's health and wellbeing.
- Commitment to equality, diversity and inclusion.
- Good IT and administrative skills.
- Willingness to work some evenings or weekends when required for events or activities.

Desirable
- Experience of working specifically with men and/or men's health.
- Experience of supporting people experiencing mental health or wellbeing challenges.
- Experience of recruiting, training or managing volunteers.
- Knowledge of local community and voluntary-sector services.
- Experience of partnership working with health, community or voluntary organisations.
- Relevant qualifications or training in health, wellbeing, community development, volunteering or a related field.
- Experience of monitoring outcomes and evaluating community programmes.

Personal Qualities

The successful candidate will be:
- Approachable and empathetic
- Positive and encouraging
- Organised and reliable
- Proactive and self-motivated
- A confident communicator
- Inclusive and non-judgemental
- Adaptable and resilient
- Passionate about improving men's health and wellbeing

What We Offer
- A rewarding opportunity to make a real difference to men's health and wellbeing.
- A supportive and friendly working environment.
- The opportunity to develop and shape Marauders' volunteer programme and wellbeing activities.
- Opportunities for professional development and training.
- The chance to work closely with volunteers, community organisations and the men we support.
- 28 days annual leave plus bank holidays! (pro rata)
- 5% pension employer contribution
- Flexible hours

Equality, Diversity and Inclusion

Marauders Men's Health Charity is committed to creating an inclusive organisation where everyone is treated with dignity, respect and fairness.

We welcome applications from people of all backgrounds and particularly encourage applications from groups that are currently underrepresented within our organisation.

Safeguarding

Marauders Men's Health Charity is committed to safeguarding the welfare of all participants, volunteers and staff. The successful candidate will be required to undertake appropriate safeguarding checks and comply with all relevant organisational policies and procedures.

How to Apply

To apply, please submit your CV and a supporting statement explaining your interest in the role, relevant experience and what you could bring to Marauders Men's Health Charity.

Closing date: October 10th
Interview date: TBC
Start date: ASAP

title: Receptionist
description: Talbot Green Group Practice are looking to recruit a full time receptionists to work within our friendly and organised team. We are a busy practice with 12,500 patients. Computer literacy skills are essential, preferably with previous experience in primary care. The successful candidates must be well organized, with excellent communication skills to deal with people in a polite and sensitive manner, and have the ability to work as part of a team.You will be part of our front of house team who are the first contact for our patients as well as undertaking daily administration tasks and responsibilities. This is a varied, rewarding and challenging role, which will suit people who are highly motivated and can cope with a demanding environment and lots of patient contact both face to face and on the telephone. You will also be expected to work in our branch surgery in Beddau so own transport is essential. The successful candidates must be well organized, with excellent communication skills to deal with people in a polite and sensitive manner, and have the ability to work as part of a team. Talbot Green Group Practice's team comprises of 5 GP Partners, 8 GP's, 3 Practice Nurses, 2 HCAs and is supported by a highly effective and friendly admin and reception team. We also have a branch surgery in Beddau. This post benefits from a generous NHS Pensions Job description You will be part of our front of house team who are the first contact for our patients as well as undertaking daily administration tasks and responsibilities. This is a varied, rewarding and challenging role, which will suit people who are highly motivated and can cope with a demanding environment and lots of patient contact both face to face and on the telephone. You will also be expected to work in our branch surgery in Beddau so own transport is essential. Hours: We have a post for a Full time 37 hours contracted weekly but (possible overtime available) between 8am and 6.30pm Monday to Friday. Must be flexible to cover for colleagues during holidays, sickness and to cover extra hours. CV and cover letter must be sent to Practice.manager.w95036@wales.nhs.uk to be considered.

title: Receptionist Administrator
location: Pontypridd, CF37 2AA, Pontypridd, CF38 1PN, Pontypridd, CF37 3DU
description: Why Join Us? This is an exciting opportunity to be part of a dynamic team at our busy town centre practice. You'll be the welcoming face of our surgery, providing essential support to patients and ensuring their healthcare journey is as smooth as possible. Heres why youll love working with us: Work-Life Balance: Monday to Friday shifts with no weekend work. Excellent Benefits Package: Including NHS pension, generous annual leave allowance, free flu jabs, uniform, and sick pay. Career Development: Were a training practice, committed to education and supporting your professional growth. Friendly Environment: Be part of a collaborative and compassionate team. What Youll Be Doing Be the first point of contact for patients both in person and over the phone. Manage appointments, process repeat prescriptions and provide general administrative support. Accurately update and maintain patient records. Collaborate with colleagues across our main and branch surgeries to deliver high-quality service. Handle queries and navigate care for patients with empathy and professionalism. DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES Provide exceptional service to our patients at the reception desk, updating computer on patients arrival and dealing with a range of routine queries including prescription requests. Problem-solve issues within competency (with senior staff always available for support). Concentration is required to deal with patients' requests and there is occasional exposure to difficult/demanding situations. Prepare consulting rooms replenishing stationery and ensuring rooms are neat and tidy. First point of contact for patients who telephone, managing appointments, dealing with routine queries, giving results etc where more senior staff are always available. Retrieve, scan and file medical records as required ensuring accuracy. Daily allocating of pathology results to appropriate GP and contacting patients as per protocol. Preparing files for all new patients. Updating practice systems with data gathered from a variety of sources e.g hospital letters, through scanning, electronic links and Cervical Screening Wales ensuring accuracy. Processing routine requests for repeat prescriptions with guidance from office manager as per protocol ensuring accuracy. Monitor registration links in accordance with practice protocol. Demonstrate duties to new staff. Participate in the development of protocols through contribution to staff meetings. Summarising of clinical records under supervision of office manager ensuring accuracy. Accept responsibility for own development and update PDP as appropriate. Liaise with and support all members of the primary care team. Alert the Management Team to issues of quality and risk.
